page_checks.summary: The garment, tool, and optical sets illustrate bipartite plural form, pair counting, dialect-specific lexical choices, and the rare singular trouser footnote.
Generic and definite-set uses contrast with variable direct counting. Specialized type and modifier uses are separate from specimen reference. Particle substances contrast with count food units.
Aggregate plurals have distinct lexical senses and partitive restrictions. Area readings of count plurals are non-individuated. The lexicalized plural inventory begins.
Lexicalized plurals cover accommodation, accumulated money, pay, social formulas, and other senses. Restricted counting and fixed predicatives are distinguished from count uses.
Borrowed and uninflected plural-only forms contrast with ordinary singulars. Rounded group counts differ from people and folk, and the section introduces singular shingles.
Singular news and disease names contrast with optional condition construals and singular measure NPs containing plural forms. The invariant count list begins.
Invariant count nouns retain their form across number. Nouns in ics show lexical number and sense distinctions, with uncertainty and agreement variation in some cases.
Game names contrast with countable pieces. Borrowed plurals vary by form and register, with lexicalized regular plurals and nonstandard overgeneralizations kept distinct.
